summary: Multiple observations of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: lack of information.
description: On November 24, 1959, at approximately 8:20 PM, a witness aboard a ship in the commercial port of Dakar, Senegal, observed a luminous phenomenon composed of points of light surrounded by a halo. This phenomenon was located to the southwest at an altitude of approximately 15 meters. The phenomenon's speed increased, and its trajectory began to descend. The halo gradually darkened, and the phenomenon disappeared. The observation lasted five minutes. In the witness's report, four ships in different locations observed the same phenomenon at roughly the same time. Only one witness account was recorded. The description of the phenomenon could suggest an aircraft in the distance, seen head-on with its landing lights on. GEIPAN classified this case as Category C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of the movement and shape changes of a luminous orange object in the sky: probable observation of a balloon.
description: On September 14, 1959, at 5:10-5:15 a.m., three witnesses south of Sali, Algeria, were intrigued by the movements of a luminous orange object in the sky. At 5:30 a.m., the object stopped moving. For 40 minutes, they observed the object drifting slowly towards the northeast, frequently changing its appearance and color (red at one end). The observation was made with binoculars. No trails or noises were observed. The observation lasted approximately one hour in total. Only one witness statement was recorded, along with two diagrams (the object's movement and changes in shape). Another observation is noted in the report. On September 12, 1959, at 7:00 p.m., an orange phenomenon with the apparent diameter of a star, located at a very high altitude and moving at high speed from 180° to 360° in approximately 30 seconds, is described. No unusual sounds were noted. Only one witness statement was collected. For the first observation, due to the duration of the observation, the slow movement, and the time close to sunrise, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of a balloon illuminated by the rising sun. The directions of observation and movement lack precision. For the observation of September 12, also reported in the witness statement, GEIPAN proposes the hypothesis of a meteoroid passing by (a brief observation of the high-speed movement of an elongated, orange luminous phenomenon at very high altitude).
